source.title: Fairness in Simple Bargaining Experiments
source.authors: Robert Forsythe, Joel L. Horowitz, N. E. Savin, Martin Sefton

studies.title: Paid extension · Five versus ten dollars

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Do people make nonzero offers because they care about fairness, or because a recipient could reject an unfair offer?

fields.label: What the paper covers
fields.value: The main experiment crosses ultimatum versus dictator rules with real versus hypothetical stakes. It is repeated across two waves, with a separate paid stake-size comparison.

fields.label: Across the paper
fields.value: Paid ultimatum and dictator offers differed. The ability to reject mattered for the observed allocation pattern; stake size in the tested range did not have a detectable effect.

fields.label: Expectation or comparison
fields.value: The fairness-alone hypothesis predicts the same distribution of offers with or without the recipient’s power to reject.

fields.label: Interpretation and limits
fields.value: Offer distributions distinguish settings with and without the power to reject. They do not identify every proposer’s motive. The no-pay ultimatum result was unstable across waves.
fields.derivation: Scope of the published evidence and, where linked, differences from the Bench adaptation.

fields.label: Participants, procedure and measures
fields.value: Anonymous participants in separate rooms played a single allocation game. In ultimatum, the recipient can accept or reject; in dictator, the recipient cannot veto. Each game was administered with and without decision-dependent payment.

fields.label: Result
fields.value: Paid ultimatum and dictator offers differed, consistent with considerations beyond fairness alone. The paid results were replicable across waves, unlike the no-pay ultimatum result.

fields.label: Participants, procedure and measures
fields.value: Compare proportions offered in paid five- and ten-dollar versions of both games. The main outcome is the distribution of offered shares.

fields.label: Result
fields.value: The authors did not find a distributional difference from doubling the pie in this range. That result does not extend to larger stakes without further evidence.
